claim: In an \(n\)-firm homogeneous-good Cournot game with constant marginal costs \(c_i\ge 0\) and a common continuous strictly decreasing inverse-demand function \(P(Q)\) satisfying \(\lim_{Q\to\infty}P(Q)=0\), every interior Cournot equilibrium is bankruptcy-free if and only if all firms have the same marginal cost.

correctness.rationale: The proof is complete under the exact stated assumptions. At an interior equilibrium every active firm has \(P(Q)>c_i\). If \(c_i<c_j\), choose \(Q'>Q\) with \(c_i<P(Q')<c_j\) and let i raise output by \(Q'-Q\); then i remains profitable and j has negative profit. If all costs equal, any price low enough to make a rival's profit negative also makes the deviator's profit negative.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For unequal active costs \(c_i<c_j\), continuity and strict decrease allow a total output \(Q'>Q\) with \(c_i<P(Q')<c_j\); firm i can increase output to \(Q'\), keep positive profit, and make firm j lose money. If all active costs equal, any price low enough to make a rival lose money also makes the deviator lose money. This proves the iff criterion directly. The result is an n-firm static classification, not a repeated-game folk theorem. The inaccessible 2024 full text leaves a possible general-characterization overlap risk.
